title: propagate-correlation-token-and-span-handoff-with-json-output-annotations
author: Lina Hoffman
description:
Motivation: Improve end-to-end observability for streaming API paths and tool/function call handlers without changing user-visible API semantics. This PR introduces a low-overhead per-request correlation token, W3C span handoff support to tool executors, and structured JSON annotations on outputs returned by the OpenAI compatibility layer. Goals: 1) ensure every top-level API request emits a stable correlation token that appears in all internal logs and in the JSON output metadata when appropriate; 2) propagate trace/span context to tool executors and any external adapters (via traceparent/tracestate) so downstream traces can be stitched with minimal sampling; 3) add compact, opt-in JSON annotations embedded in streaming chunks for safe machine parsing by customers and monitoring backends; 4) emit periodic lightweight heartbeat events for long-running streams so metrics systems can attribute duration correctly. Implementation summary:
- Adds a lightweight header X-Redwood-Corr (also accepted as Redwood-Corr) generated at the gateway layer when missing; mapped to log field corr_token and to the output annotation redwood.corr_token.
- Introduces span_handoff middleware that extracts W3C traceparent and serializes a minimal span_context into function/tool-call envelopes so third-party tool executors and on-prem agents can create child spans. span_handoff is pluggable and no-op when downstream doesn't accept trace headers.
- Streaming changes: annotate the first chunk of a stream with a stable "redwood_meta" JSON object containing corr_token, endpoint_id, model_variant and a small schema_version. Subsequent chunks may include a 1-line delta annotation (chunk_seq) when enabled via query param or SDK flag. Annotation emission is opt-in and guarded by a feature flag to avoid payload bloat for customers that don't need machine-readable stream metadata.
- Logging: structured JSON logs now include top-level fields corr_token, endpoint, model_variant, and stream_chunk_seq when present. Logs for function/tool calls include tool_id and callable_span_context for easy correlation.
- Metrics: per-endpoint dimensional tags are attached to the latency and token_count metrics (endpoint_id, compatibility_mode=openai|native). Also added a small histogram for stream idle time to help debug stuck streams. Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- No breaking changes to the public REST contract; X-Redwood-Corr is optional if callers already provide a correlation token.
- Feature gated: annotations default to off; rollout via console flags and staged canaries.
- Added integration tests that simulate tool executors responding with resumed span_context and verify parent-child linkage in traces. Security and privacy: correlation tokens are random opaque 128-bit values and are not user-identifying; we avoid including any PII in annotations. The PR includes docs and an upgrade note for private deployments. Related items: linear ENG-1423 (stream stability metrics), ENG-1489 (openai-compat annotations).
commits: 4 commits: 1) wire: add corr token header generation in gateway and map to request context; 2) runtime: span_handoff middleware to package traceparent for tool executors; 3) openai-adapter: include redwood_meta annotation on first stream chunk and optional chunk_seq; 4) observability: structured log fields, metrics dimensions, tests and docs updates.

release_notes: Added correlation token propagation (X-Redwood-Corr), optional JSON stream annotations (redwood_meta) for machine-parseable metadata, span handoff for tool executors to allow end-to-end trace stitching, and per-endpoint observability dimensions. Annotations are feature-flagged and off by default.
